req.title: Reject non-GET on /get
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for any non-GET request to /get.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /get must accept GET requests (HTTP 200) and reject all non-GET methods with HTTP 405. Tests cover: (1) positive path — GET returns 200 with expected JSON keys; (2) negative paths — POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary — HEAD and OPTIONS (edge-case methods) also return 405. Assertions use exact status codes and exact JSON key presence to kill constant-mutation and comparison-flip mutants. Both sides of the method-allow decision are exercised.

tests.name: test_get_request_returns_200_with_expected_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Test client is created from app
expected: Response body is JSON containing keys: url, args, headers, origin
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_request_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data
    assert 'form' not in data
    assert 'files' not in data

test_get_request_returns_200_with_expected_payload()

tests.name: test_all_non_get_methods_return_exactly_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Test client is created from app
actions: Send POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and HEAD to /get
trace: R-HTTPBIN-003: exhaustive non-GET method coverage -> all 405
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_non_get_methods_return_exactly_405():
    methods = [
        client.post,
        client.put,
        client.patch,
        client.delete,
    ]
    for method_fn in methods:
        r = method_fn('/get')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"Expected 405 but got {r.status_code} for {method_fn}"
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 400
        assert r.status_code != 500

test_all_non_get_methods_return_exactly_405()

tests.name: test_get_returns_200_not_405_boundary
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Test client is created from app
actions: Send GET to /get (the only allowed method)
Assert status is exactly 200 and not 405
trace: R-HTTPBIN-003: GET is the boundary between allowed and disallowed methods
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_returns_200_not_405_boundary():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 405
    assert r.status_code != 404
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert set(['url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin']).issubset(set(data.keys()))

test_get_returns_200_not_405_boundary()

Test client is created from app
expected: Response JSON args contains foo=bar and baz=42
trace: R-HTTPBIN-003: GET /get with query params -> 200 with args reflected
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_with_query_params_returns_200_and_args():
    r = client.get('/get?foo=bar&baz=42')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert data['args'] == {'foo': 'bar', 'baz': '42'}
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data
